Subject: ACME RAG eval — follow-up & recommended next steps

Hi Alice / Ben,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and helpful context on the datasets you plan to index (sales docs + product FAQs + policy manuals). Quick recap and recommended next steps from our side: 

- Recap from demo: RAG prototype performed well on recall for product FAQs but we saw some precision/hallucination concerns on policy language.
- Immediate wins: tune retriever overlap to reduce near-duplicate snippets, add an explicit reranker for grounding-sensitive responses.
- Recommended models to evaluate: Redwood-2-Chat (v1, 16k) and Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized int8) for baseline latency/cost, evaluate Mistral-Instruct-7B for constrained budgets.

I've attached a short summary (acme_rag_eval_summary.pdf), the prompt set we used (prompt_set_acme_v2.txt), retriever snippets (retriever_config_snippets.json) and raw benchmark results (acme_benchmark_results.xlsx). Key metrics to watch: grounding rate (fraction of claims supported by retrieved docs), top-1 precision, and false-positive hallucination rate on policy questions.

Next steps / asks: 
1) Can you confirm which production index you want to prioritize (product_faqs vs. policies) — suggested: start with product_faqs to get quick wins.
2) Please share a small sample of the most-common user query types (5-10 examples) so we can refine prompts and reranker thresholds.
3) If OK, we'll schedule a 30-min deep-dive with Vivek to review retriever/reranker config and run a short A/B with the two model variants next week.

Proposed times: Tue 3/17 10:00-10:30 or Wed 3/18 14:00-14:30 PT — let me know what works.

Thanks,

—Marissa

Perfect — thanks for confirming, Alice. Tue 3/17 10:00 PT is on our side. I'm looping in Vivek (solutions engineering) to lead the technical portion and walk through the configuration and quick A/B plan. Vivek — attaching the summary and prompts we used for context.

High level answers to Alice's two questions: 
- Reranker: start with a distilled bi-encoder reranker (cost-effective) for the product_faqs pilot. For the policies index, we recommend a cross-encoder reranker for stricter grounding (apply only to a small set of policy-critical queries to limit cost).
- Thresholds: initial similarity threshold: cosine similarity >= 0.78 (dense embedding space) to filter obviously irrelevant passages. For reranker score cut: top-k=5 for retriever, then rerank top-5 with cross-encoder (if used) and require reranker_score >= 0.45 for answers that cite policy docs; otherwise fall back to model-only answer with a "low-confidence" flag.

We'll review these numbers and adjust during the session; they are conservative starting points based on the benchmark results in the attachment.

See you all Tue 3/17 10:00 PT. Vivek — can you add any notes / technical checklist below?

—Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: ACME RAG eval — technical notes & A/B checklist

Hi Alice / Ben / Marissa,

Thanks for looping me in. Quick technical notes and the A/B checklist for Tue's session. I've included concrete config snippets (see retriever_config_snippets.json attachment) and the short plan we'll execute live.

Key recommendations (concise):
1) Retriever: dense hybrid (BM25 + vector) with stop-word trimming for short queries. Retriever params to start: top_k=100, vector_similarity=cosine, similarity_threshold=0.78. Use passage-level chunks of ~250 tokens with 128-token overlap.

2) Reranker strategy: 
  - Pilot (product_faqs): Distilled bi-encoder reranker (fast) applied to top-100 -> shortlist top-5. Use reranker_score threshold 0.40 for surfaced passages.
  - Policy-critical flows: Cross-encoder reranker for final verification on top-5 passages; require cross-encoder score >= 0.45 to allow the assistant to assert a policy claim; otherwise the assistant must respond with a grounded disclaimer and cite sources.

3) Model selection & A/B: 
  - A: Redwood-2-Chat (v1, 16k context) — expected higher grounding with slightly higher cost.
  - B: Llama-2-13B-chat (int8 quantized) — lower cost, similar latency; expect slightly higher hallucination on policy-edge cases.
  - Metrics to collect: grounding_rate (claims with supporting citation), precision@1, recall@5, hallucination_rate (false positives on a curated policy prompt set), latency P50/P95, tokens/call cost.

4) Evaluation harness: run 200 query eval across both models and both reranker configs (bi-encoder vs cross-encoder for policy queries). We'll produce a simple confusion matrix for grounding vs hallucination and a per-query breakdown in the benchmark spreadsheet.

5) Rollout recommendations: start with product_faqs using pipeline: retriever (top-100) -> bi-encoder reranker -> top-5 -> Redwood-2-Chat (A). If policy query detected (simple keyword classifier), switch to the cross-encoder verification path.

Action items for Tue session: 
- ACME: share 8 sample queries (Alice) + indicator of policy-critical query types.
- Redwood: run the 200-query eval overnight with the configs above and share results in Drive before the meeting.
- Schedule: 3/17 10:00 PT (meet link will be sent).

I've attached the retriever config snippets and the prompt set we used. If you want, I can also export a small Jupyter notebook that runs the A/B locally against your sample queries (requires a short token for sandbox access).

Thanks, looking forward to the session.

—Vivek Kulkarni
